markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize **causal recent–consensus fusion**: a small SASRec residual that separates current behavior from sustained preferences while limiting the influence of isolated interactions.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already supports causal contextualization; an auxiliary branch must demonstrate value beyond additional capacity [1]. (2) Electronics’ 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and −0.4812 lower-tail margin motivate improving candidate separation, but do not establish validation gains. (3) Similar embedding-similarity scores across datasets do not explain their ranking differences; indiscriminate decorrelation lacks diagnostic justification.

**Insights from related work.** (1) LSIDN motivates separating short-term intent from sustained interests rather than pooling them indiscriminately [2]. (2) BSARec motivates retaining both stable and changing signals, without treating frequency components as observed intent [3]. (3) gSASRec supplies an independent objective control: stronger negative supervision may matter more than another representation branch [4]. Historical transition variants scored 0.5200–0.5287, but those scores do not isolate their mechanisms.

The framework separates three research directions:

| Direction | Mechanism | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal evidence | Recent and prefix-wide causal pools | Genuine intent changes versus isolated actions |
| Ranking supervision | Multi-negative generalized BCE | Transfer from training margins to HR@10 |
| Population evidence | Supported directed transitions | Sparse independent edge coverage |

Three atomic candidates follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means more effort.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Recent–consensus fusion [1–3] | 3/7/7/6/3 | O: focused synthesis, established components. P: reusable temporal control, coarse windows. U: addresses stale interests and isolated evidence, cannot verify utility. M: changes confusing states, margin gains uncertain. D: compact pooling/gate, causal export needs care. |
| Multi-negative gBCE [4] | 2/7/5/8/4 | O: clean control, published method. P: broad applicability, sampling dependence. U: may improve matches, no explicit intent mechanism. M: directly trains discrimination, diagnostic negatives differ. D: compact loss, added memory. |
| User-excluded transition residual | 3/6/6/6/6 | O: precise support handling, established rules. P: interpretable evidence, sparse coverage. U: supported continuations, no compatibility proof. M: candidate corrections, unsupported pairs unchanged. D: small scorer, substantial provenance integration. |

**Selected algorithm.** Pool item embeddings over the latest five interactions and the complete available prefix. A small gate uses the SASRec state and agreement between the latest item and these pools; a bounded residual adds their weighted representation before candidate scoring. This explicitly targets **older broad interests overriding recent intent** and **isolated interactions being overinterpreted as preference**. It also targets Electronics’ weak separation through the unchanged ranking loss. These are hypotheses; coherence must not be interpreted as calibrated confidence or dislike.

Compare baseline, fixed equal fusion, and adaptive fusion under matched compute. Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, routing, epoch defaults, diagnostic contracts, and identical exported scoring. No improvement is claimed.

References: [1] SASRec; [2] LSIDN; [3] BSARec; [4] gSASRec; links below.

idea.description: Add a bounded causal recent–consensus representation residual to each dataset-specific SASRec. At each position, form recent-five and full-available-prefix means of the backbone item embeddings. A two-way gate conditions on the SASRec state and agreement of the current item with each pool. Mix the pools, normalize the result, and add a small bounded residual to the SASRec state before the existing candidate dot product.
idea.motivation: The selected mechanism addresses two user-observed failures: older broad interests overriding current intent, and isolated interactions receiving more preference weight than their evidence warrants. Recent pooling supplies a current-context alternative; prefix pooling supplies a sustained-context alternative; their gate can learn which better predicts subsequent interactions. This does not establish compatibility, equipment ownership, replacement needs, or whether a need has already been satisfied. The model-facing target is weak positive–negative separation, particularly Electronics’ 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and negative margin p10. These training diagnostics motivate the experiment but cannot predict validation improvement.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use histories only for this first experiment. Do not use unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores, simulator traits, external data, or pretrained weights. The supplied metadata examples do not authorize those fields.

Define x_t as the unscaled item-table embedding before position embeddings and dropout. Compute masked causal means R_t over the latest five nonpadding interactions and P_t over the available prefix through t. Use prefix sums and valid-count denominators; set empty pools to zero. The full prefix means the history available after baseline truncation, not interactions outside the provided sequence. All pooling inputs and gate features must be prefix-only.

Let z_t concatenate h_t, cosine(x_t,R_t), cosine(x_t,P_t), and log1p(valid_prefix_length). Compute g_t=softmax(W z_t+b), v_t=g_t[0]R_t+g_t[1]P_t, and f_t=h_t+a*v_t/max(norm(v_t),1e-8). Set a=2*sigmoid(theta), initialized to 0.01. Initialize W and b to zero, giving equal initial mixing. Mask the residual at padding positions. The residual representation norm is at most two; candidate-logit changes are not uniformly bounded because item-vector norms vary. Include theta in an optimizer group without weight decay, leaving baseline groups unchanged. The constants are initial engineering settings, not measured optima.

Preserve baseline architecture, loss, optimizer settings, sampler, examples and preprocessing for the first comparison. Compare three variants: unchanged SASRec, identical residual with fixed equal mixing, and adaptive mixing. The fixed-mixing control retains the same learned amplitude. Allocate at most 12,000 GPU-seconds per variant across four categories, equally divided, reserving 7,200 seconds for all validation, diagnostics, debugging and failures. Stop each category at 200 epochs, the SASREC_EPOCHS environment override, or its 3,000-second cap, whichever occurs first. Use one complete four-category checkpoint bundle per variant for primary selection. Log charged time, updates and effective epochs; equal time may yield different update counts. Any necessary schedule revision must precede comparative execution and validation inspection.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, and int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS','200')). Save architecture configuration, parameters, mappings and logs beneath the trial directory. Keep execution single-GPU. Generate working/predict.py using the identical model implementation and configuration. Inference requires no additional metadata or sparse statistics.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and the public loader tuple (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. view.model must reference the complete trained module, and view.item_emb the backbone item table. log2feats returns the final augmented B x L x D tensor, so predict_score remains a dot product and the initial tensor compatibility contract is retained. Compute original margin diagnostics through the complete scorer. Report gate weights, amplitude, residual norms, and backbone-versus-augmented margins on identical diagnostic batches. Define embedding similarity as a property of the backbone table, not the whole scoring function. Mark unavailable category and review analyses explicitly unavailable.

Verify causal prefix invariance, left padding, short histories, truncation, zero residual, checkpoint reloads, all category routes, and candidate-versus-chunked-full-catalog score agreement. Compare training-inference and exported float32 scores with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4; investigate any top-10 disagreement. Preserve host evaluation and masking behavior. Run the required twenty-user unseen-item simulator protocol, five users per category, and examine recent-intent matches and unsupported preference extrapolation separately from equipment assumptions. Select only by the pinned macro validation HR@10; exact ties prefer baseline, then fixed mixing. Freeze the winner before separate held-out evaluation. No experiments or improvements are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
epoch_limit = int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200'))

for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    preserve_baseline_preprocessing(seed=0)
    set_training_seed(42)
    model = DatasetSASRecWithCausalFusion(config)

    def log2feats(sequence):
        valid = sequence != 0
        h = backbone.log2feats(sequence)
        x = item_emb(sequence) * valid[..., None]
        recent = masked_causal_mean(x, valid, window=5)
        prefix = masked_causal_mean(x, valid, window='available_prefix')
        length = cumsum(valid, dim=1)
        gate_input = concat(h, cosine(x, recent), cosine(x, prefix), log1p(length))
        weights = softmax(linear(gate_input), dim=-1)
        # Fixed control uses weights=(0.5, 0.5).
        pooled = weights[..., 0:1] * recent + weights[..., 1:2] * prefix
        direction = pooled / clamp_min(norm(pooled, dim=-1, keepdim=True), 1e-8)
        amplitude = 2 * sigmoid(theta)  # initialized to 0.01
        return (h + amplitude * direction) * valid[..., None]

    def predict_score(features, items):
        return broadcasted_dot(features, item_emb(items))

    for _, sequence, positive, negative in baseline_train_loader:
        features = log2feats(sequence)
        pos = predict_score(features, positive)
        neg = predict_score(features, negative)
        loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(pos, neg, valid=positive != 0)
        optimize(loss)
        enforce_epoch_and_charged_compute_caps()

    save_complete_model_mapping_and_config_under_trial_directory()
    write_predictor_with_identical_model_and_scoring()
    verify_causality_reload_and_scoring_parity()
    run_required_diagnostics_and_simulator()

# Compare baseline, fixed fusion, adaptive fusion.
# Select solely by unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10.
# Charge all search GPU work to the shared 43,200-second budget.

originality.positive: A minimal gate connects recent-versus-sustained evidence directly to two diagnosed user failures while preserving the SASRec feature contract.
originality.negative: Temporal pooling, adaptive fusion and residual sequential representations are established; the proposal is a controlled adaptation rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: Provides a low-cost framework for testing when recent context or sustained behavior should influence recommendations, without requiring repeated population transitions.
future_potential.negative: Learned agreement may reinforce broad interests or suppress genuine new interests; it cannot verify practical usefulness or compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires causal pooling, a small linear gate and one amplitude while retaining tensor-valued features and ordinary dot-product scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding, causal alignment, export parity, compute accounting and meaningful simulator comparisons still require careful integration.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention backbone and candidate dot-product scoring starting point.
limitations: Its architecture alone does not explicitly distinguish recent intent from sustained preference.
The supplied diagnosis does not establish that attention is the cause of the observed errors.

related_work.title: LSIDN
contributions: Motivates separating long-term interest evolution and short-term intent with distinct denoising mechanisms.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this lightweight pooling adaptation under the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: BSARec
contributions: Motivates preserving stable and changing representation components through frequency-aware sequential modeling.
limitations: Frequency components are modeling proxies rather than observed intent labels.
Its results do not validate the proposed gate or diagnose collapse in these datasets.

related_work.title: gSASRec author implementation
contributions: Provides generalized BCE and multi-negative training as an independent objective-focused alternative.
limitations: Objective changes alone do not explicitly model recent intent or uncertainty from isolated interactions.
Accuracy and compute effects require matched validation in this task.
